LEAD | program: shortwin | function: sync_lender | bug_class: repeated-accrual-truncation | group_key: shortwin | sync_lender | repeated-accrual-truncation
file: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sync_lender.rs:126
related: crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:1473
status: Known lead strengthened with a concrete bounded two-release trace; material aggregate harm remains unproven.
code_smells: The current-epoch path floors each share credit separately and then advances both snapshots; it stores no fractional lender remainder.
description: Any caller can discard a lender's fractional SOL credits through repeated syncs; material aggregate harm remains unproven.
proof: Two lenders deposit one raw token each before any lump. pool.rs:1720-1726 mints 1000 shares for each, total_shares=2000. All snapshots and balances start at zero. A genuine two-lamport trader sweep vests the two lamports through sweep_trader.rs:359-370 and pool.rs:2200-2225. Use the default lump_vest_s=21,600 (params.rs:213) and calls after 10,800 and 21,600 seconds; with no intervening pool accruals, release_in at pool.rs:898-928 releases exactly one lamport at each call. A zero-value sweep invokes prologue::accrue before its own zero sweep (sweep_trader.rs:310; prologue.rs:119), so it can release the existing vest without a venue quote or new borrowed position.
proof: Each released lamport adds exactly 10^18/2000=500,000,000,000,000 to acc and acc_r, with pool-level carries zero. After the first release, an outsider supplies the genuine market, vault, victim lender and victim owner accounts to sync_lender(0), with no owner signature and no remaining epoch accounts. The instruction explicitly permits the unsigned path at sync_lender.rs:118-132. With the lender current and fwd=FWD_NONE, touch_pot at pool.rs:1667-1685 reaches touch_tail. At 1474-1475 it adds floor(1000*500,000,000,000,000/10^18)=0 to pending and real. Lines 1487-1488 nevertheless set snap and snap_r to the current accumulators. After the second release, another unsigned sync again adds zero and advances the snapshots. The victim receives zero. Without the midpoint sync, the victim receives floor(1000*1,000,000,000,000,000/10^18)=1 lamport. Both the entitlement and realized allocation lose this lamport; to_pot sees no surplus in this trace and does not restore it. The other lender can still receive its own one lamport; the lost lamport remains tracked in the vault.
limits: At fixed shares, each floor can discard less than one lamport per accumulator per touch. The worked complete trace destroys one payable lamport after two releases. No larger economically material aggregate, profitable attack, direct attacker payout, or significant negative-pending lockout has been proved. Repeating calls without an intervening accumulator change adds no loss. Pool-level carry and rent::lender_credit_carried do not preserve the per-lender fractions. Source comments intentionally specify flooring; the unresolved question is the effect of third-party-selected snapshot intervals, not whether integer division floors.
fix_direction: Preserve fractional entitlement and realized-credit remainders per lender across touches, share changes and epoch conversion. The forward-chain path already uses cumulative floors (pool.rs:1403-1407), but copying that formula into the ordinary path requires analysis: deposit and withdraw change shares after the touch and snapshot update, so their new share counts choose a new absolute rounding phase. No unvalidated cumulative-floor patch is proposed.
funding_note: Each tiny trader donation and sweep can share one transaction; engine/trader.rs:139-183 checks a System-owned empty trader and transfers its entire balance to the rent-exempt market vault, leaving the trader at zero. The trace does not require a persistent under-rent account.
verification: Static source trace and integer arithmetic only; no build, test, program execution or runtime reproduction.

title: Exit instructions omit the position status check
file: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/close_short.rs:82
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/liquidate.rs:123; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/expire.rs:93; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sol_settle.rs:122; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/add_margin.rs:63; programs/shortwin/src/state/position.rs:18
code_smells: AddMargin requires position.status == POSITION_OPEN, but CloseShort, Liquidate, Expire, and SolSettle do not.
description: A future instruction that sets POSITION_EXIT_IN_PROGRESS can leave its position eligible for close_short and keeper exits because those paths omit status checks.
limits: This is not an exploit in the reviewed build. POSITION_EXIT_IN_PROGRESS is reserved for v1.1, and open_short currently writes only POSITION_OPEN. The independent gate already exists in add_margin; the other four Accounts structs check the account's borrower, market, and PDA but not its status. A future non-open state must be excluded explicitly before this omission becomes reachable.
fix: Add the POSITION_OPEN constraint to each exit instruction before any instruction writes another live position status.

code_smells: The pool_vault constraints check its PDA, but omit token::mint, token::authority, and token::token_program.
trace: Deposit binds the market to mint, pool_vault, and token_program, then loads pool_vault as InterfaceAccount<TokenAccount>. Withdraw and the short instructions use the same vault pattern. Token CPIs and trader post-conditions add downstream checks. No current counterfeit-vault path was proved.
description: A future vault migration can admit the wrong token fields because deposit checks the vault address without explicit token field constraints.
fix: Add token mint, authority, and program constraints to each pool_vault load.

title: Exit handlers omit the position status check
code_smells: The four exit handlers check the position address and relationships but omit its status; add_margin checks POSITION_OPEN.
description: A future migration can expose non-open positions to exit handlers because those handlers do not check the status.
input: A caller supplies a genuine program-owned ShortPosition with a future status other than POSITION_OPEN, plus its correct market, borrower, and exposure.
assumption: Every correctly addressed ShortPosition that reaches an exit remains open.
path: A future instruction writes POSITION_EXIT_IN_PROGRESS -> close_short, liquidate, expire, or sol_settle loads the genuine position -> the handler applies its normal exit accounting.
proof: ShortPosition defines POSITION_OPEN=0 and reserves POSITION_EXIT_IN_PROGRESS=1 at state/position.rs:19-21. The four exit account structs check has_one and position.is_pda but never position.status. Their handlers copy the position and proceed directly to settlement or buyback calculations. add_margin.rs:65 demonstrates the missing defensive comparison. A cross-file search found open_short.rs:616 as the only production status assignment, and it writes POSITION_OPEN.
guards: Anchor checks the account owner and discriminator. The position PDA, market, borrower, and exposure bindings prevent a caller from fabricating the future status. All financial guards still apply. The current program never writes the reserved status. Anchor 1.2.0 closes an account by assigning System ownership and resizing to zero; its account exit skips a closed account, so this is not a current account-revival path.
impact_and_limitations: This is a future-state hardening gap. No current attacker can create the required position state through the reviewed instructions. No current double close, double payout, or loss is proved.
fix: Require POSITION_OPEN in each exit account struct before the handler uses the position.
proposed_diff: Unapplied and uncompiled; this adds the same defensive check to each affected exit.

location: shortwin::inputs
title: Temporary withdrawals change the live settlement legs
code_smells: The spot gate uses the EMA liquidity floor, but the S1 and S2 legs use live liquidity from the caller's transaction.
description: An LP can change settlement legs through temporary withdrawals; borrower loss outside the documented residual remains unproved.
input: An unlocked LP supplies a valid sol_settle instruction between its venue withdrawal and redeposit. The position is already expired or passes both liquidation gates.
assumption: The box corner rejects harmful changes to the live settlement legs even when the honest live state lies outside the box.
path: Venue withdrawal -> sol_settle reads reduced reserves -> inputs retains reduced l_live and the reduced-reserve live quote -> S1/S2 evaluates those values and the unchanged box corner -> the transaction restores liquidity after the settlement call.
proof: inputs reads state.liquidity at arming.rs:208 and computes b_live and sigma_live from state.x/state.y at lines 214-220. It computes the protected l_spot separately at line 223. SettleInputs still receives the original l_live at line 259. settle::s1_legs checks both b_live and quotes.cost(p_rs,l_live), and s2_legs checks sigma_live and quotes.sigma(p_rs,l_live). The refutation uses min(l_live,bx.l_lo), so a withdrawal cannot help refute. These reads occur before any venue CPI; they reflect all earlier instructions in the same transaction. This independently confirms control of those inputs, not a profitable attack.
conditional_arithmetic: At price 1, an exact-out fee-free quote for q=100 from reserves (1000,1000) costs ceil(1000*100/900)=112. A proportional withdrawal to (200,200) raises it to 200. If the box's least-favorable S1 corner remains (P=1,L=200), ert=0, and V-K_s=150, all three S1 legs hold only during the withdrawal. This illustrates the predicate change. It does not establish that this complete account state satisfies the protocol's open caps or that the state persists for the required updates.
guards: The CR spot gate floors liquidity at spot_liquidity, and the EMA leg also applies. The expired alternative still applies. Warm-up, a fresh robust spot, the independent box corner, the arming gap, restart_ema_count, and settle_persist_n remain required. Repeated calls in one second cannot create the required EMA updates. S2 and S3 also require the box amount check. Failed later instructions revert the settlement and withdrawal together.
impact_and_limitations: An LP can affect arming or settlement only if the independent box corner already permits it and the honest live state lies outside that box. arming.rs:41-54 explicitly documents this AIR-20 residual, including the reported absence of borrower loss at default parameters. This pass establishes no new exploit outside that stated residual and does not promote the lead to a finding. No runtime reproduction was performed.
fix: Compare reachable borrower payouts before any change to the documented live-liquidity leg rules.
remediation_limit: No code diff is proposed because an EMA floor on these legs changes the stated economic design and this pass proves no new loss.

title: Repeated sync calls discard fractional lender credits
location: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sync_lender.rs:119-130
related_locations: crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:1459-1502,1660-1695
code_smells: touch_tail floors each current-epoch accrual and then advances both snapshots. An unsigned caller can invoke that path for another lender.
description: An outsider can discard a lender's fractional credits through repeated sync calls; this review does not establish a profitable transaction schedule.
invariant: For fixed shares, splitting a lender update should preserve its accumulated entitlement and realised allocation within a single final rounding unit.
proof: For a current lender with 1000 of 3000 shares, three separate one-lamport global credits produce accumulator increments of 333333333333333, 333333333333333, and 333333333333334. A touch after each credits floor(1000*increment/10^18)=0 every time and overwrites snap. A single touch after all three credits one lamport. Over 300 one-lamport credits, separate touches give zero while one final touch gives 100 lamports. The same arithmetic applies to acc_r when those credits are realised. sync_lender with owner.is_signer=false calls touch_pot, which reaches touch_tail for a current lender. The rebase authorization guard does not prevent this current-epoch path.
guards_and_limits: Repeating sync without an intervening accumulator change is idempotent. The forward-chain path uses cumulative floors and avoids this particular loss. This review does not establish live credit timing, transaction costs, or a direct attacker payout from the lost entitlement. Source comments prescribe floor rounding, but do not establish that outsiders should erase a lender's accumulated fractions repeatedly.
fix: Preserve each lender's fractional accrual remainder, or use cumulative entitlement differences across snapshots without a share change.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: deposit | bug_class: donation-extends-deposit-hold | group_key: shortwin | deposit | donation-extends-deposit-hold
title: Small donations can extend a settlement hold
location: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/deposit.rs:130-135
related_locations: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sol_settle.rs:336-342; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sweep_trader.rs:351-383; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:948-999,2200-2230
code_smells: A settlement arms deposit_hold_until, but deposit tests the shared vest balance. Anyone can add another lump through sweep_trader.
description: An outsider can extend a settlement's deposit hold with small donations; this review leaves the intended donation policy unresolved.
invariant: A hold introduced for pre-deposit settlement income should end after that income releases, unless the protocol explicitly gives outsiders control over the hold.
proof: Consider S>0, deposit_hold_until>=0, both sweep bits already set, and a settlement vest whose balance has one lamport left. With lump_vest_s=21600, at one second before vest_end the old one-lamport balance releases zero. A one-lamport trader donation followed by sweep_trader adds a second lamport and computes the new remaining span as floor((1*1+1*21600)/2)=10800 seconds. deposit continues to fail PoolDrained while vest_bal>0, irrespective of the original recorded hold end. A donation at the original end can release the old balance and start a new one-lamport vest before a deposit runs. Repetition requires successful transaction ordering, but does not require a lender or borrower signature.
guards_and_limits: A pending first trader sweep after a dust flush uses immediate credit and does not extend the vest. The trace starts after that source bit is set, or from an ordinary held settlement. last-share withdrawal and a subsequent full vest flush can end the hold. Source comments deliberately require the shared vest to reach zero because later income can extend its end; they do not resolve whether arbitrary donations may perpetuate that restriction. This remains a policy-sensitive lead.
fix: Track the release of settlement income separately from new discretionary donations before the program releases the deposit hold.

LEAD | program: shortwin | function: deposit | bug_class: donation-extends-deposit-hold | group_key: shortwin | deposit | donation-extends-deposit-hold
title: Small donations can extend a settlement hold
file: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/deposit.rs:130-135; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sol_settle.rs:322-329; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sweep_trader.rs:184,282-291,358-370; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:898-928,948-988,2200-2229
pair_or_branch: settlement-created deposit hold / unrelated trader donation; fixed stored marker / live shared vest
asymmetry: sol_settle records a hold from settlement vesting; deposit waits for the entire current vest balance, including later trader donations.
code_smells: The deposit guard uses deposit_hold_until only as a flag and blocks on pool.vest_bal instead of a settlement-specific balance.
proof: sol_settle.rs:322-329 can leave deposit_hold_until nonnegative after a nonflushed settlement. deposit.rs:130-135 clears that marker only when an attempted deposit observes vest_bal == 0. SweepTrader has no signer requirement and normalises donated lamports before pool::sweep. engine/trader.rs:142-183 moves the trader's full lamport balance into market_vault. pool.rs:2200-2229 passes ordinary trader sweeps to vest_in when shares remain and the source has no after-flush immediate-credit entitlement. Suppose a held market's old vest ends at t0, no deposit has yet cleared its marker, and shares remain. A donation followed by sweep_trader at t0 first releases the old vest, then creates a new vest. With one donated lamport and lump_vest_s = 21600, vest_in sets vest_bal = 1 and vest_end = t0 + 21600. A deposit at t0 + 1 computes floor(1 / 21600) = 0 in release_in, leaves vest_bal = 1 and returns PoolDrained. The stale hold marker therefore blocks deposits after the original settlement vest ends.
guards: The market must already have an active hold, must retain shares, and must not have cleared the marker through a successful deposit. The after-flush immediate-credit branch must not apply. The value-weighted formula prevents arbitrary end extensions from dust while a large vest remains. Withdrawals and claims remain available.
impact: A caller may extend the period during which new lenders cannot deposit through a small unrelated donation.
limitations: This remains an economic and liveness lead. The review did not establish an attacker profit model or reproduce the exact low-value donation transaction under runtime rent checks. The source explicitly protects later extensions of the shared vest, but does not state whether repeated unrelated donations should extend the admission hold.
description: A donor may extend a settlement hold through unrelated vesting; the review leaves the intended admission policy and exact donation cost unverified.
fix: Track the protected settlement vest separately so unrelated donations cannot prolong its deposit hold.

assumption: A nondefault, distinct successor key identifies an authority that can use the role.
actual: The handler replaces governance, pause_authority, and coverage_authority without a signature from any successor.
path: Honest governance proposes a mistaken successor G_bad; the timelock elapses; any caller applies the proposal; G_bad becomes governance.
proof: Set G_bad = config.key(), the existing canonical PDA derived from [GlobalConfig::SEED] under shortwin. No production instruction signs governance calls with that PDA. Keep pause_authority, coverage_authority, and fee_recipient distinct and otherwise valid. check_authorities rejects zero and duplicate keys, but it does not authenticate G_bad. propose_config accepts the old governance signature. apply_config checks pending existence, not_before, the 14-day application window, and parameter validity. It calls c.apply and c.pending.clear without any successor account or signature. GlobalConfig::apply assigns self.governance = *governance. The fee_recipient account can remain the valid existing System account, so its additional check passes. The old governance then fails propose_config's equality constraint. The Emergency authority cannot propose a replacement and cannot cancel an Authorities change under cancel_config. No protocol instruction restores the governance key.
guards_and_limits: An outsider cannot create or alter the proposal. The old governance must make an honest address error and fail to cancel it before execution. A program upgrade can repair the state. Public execution of an authenticated proposal is intentional; the defect is the absent successor acceptance.
impact: An honest authority rotation can disable all later governance changes until a program upgrade.
description: Governance can install an unusable successor without its signature, so later governance changes fail until a program upgrade.
fix: Require each changed, nondefault authority to sign before the handler applies an Authorities change.
minimal_diff: The diff is proposed only. It uses remaining accounts for successor signatures and requires matching client metadata.
```diff
--- a/programs/shortwin/src/instructions/apply_config.rs
+++ b/programs/shortwin/src/instructions/apply_config.rs
@@ -77,6 +77,28 @@
         let change = c.pending.change()?;
         c.check_change(&change)?;
         let applied = (c.pending.kind, c.pending.hash());
+        if let ConfigChange::Authorities {
+            governance,
+            pause_authority,
+            coverage_authority,
+            ..
+        } = &change
+        {
+            for (current, next) in [
+                (c.governance, *governance),
+                (c.pause_authority, *pause_authority),
+                (c.coverage_authority, *coverage_authority),
+            ] {
+                if next != Pubkey::default() && next != current {
+                    require!(
+                        ctx.remaining_accounts
+                            .iter()
+                            .any(|account| account.key() == next && account.is_signer),
+                        ShortwinError::Unauthorized
+                    );
+                }
+            }
+        }
         c.apply(&change, clock.unix_timestamp)?;
         c.pending.clear();
         (applied.0, applied.1, change)
```

title: Small donations can renew a settlement hold
location: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/deposit.rs:130-135; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sol_settle.rs:325-328; programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sweep_trader.rs:275-284, 306-386; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:898-1003
seam: execution×periphery×first-principles
code_smells: The deposit hold follows the entire shared vest, including later unsolicited SOL.
description: An outsider can renew a settlement hold with a small donation; the review does not establish a guaranteed long-term block.
trace: A settlement sets deposit_hold_until and leaves S>0 → original vest reaches its end → outsider funds trader and calls sweep_trader → a fresh vest prevents deposit.
proof: deposit checks only whether the marker is nonnegative, then requires pool.vest_bal==0. It does not clear the marker merely because its recorded timestamp passed. At the original vest end, sweep_trader's prologue releases the original balance; its subsequent sweep of one lamport starts a fresh vest. The default lump_vest_s is 21,600 seconds. The marker remains nonnegative because only a successful deposit resets it. A deposit in that interval fails PoolDrained even though the original settlement vest completed. The same sequence can repeat at the next end if the outsider lands before a deposit. On an already-running vest, floor rounding limits small donations: the review does not claim that each lamport always extends the end.
guards: The market must already have a hold and surviving shares. The sweep must satisfy its stored trader keys and applicable token-leg accounts. An ordinary market with deposit_hold_until=-1 does not acquire this hold from a simple donation. A final lender withdrawal can flush the vest; a deposit that lands first at release can clear the marker.
limitations: The source explicitly requires later legitimate credits to remain protected until the shared vest empties. This lead concerns unsolicited donations and timing around the end, not an incorrect timestamp comparison. A sustained block and its economic impact remain unverified.
fix_direction: Separate the amount protected by a settlement hold from later unsolicited donations while preserving the old holders' pending cashback.

title: Repeated sync calls discard fractional lender credits
location: programs/shortwin/src/instructions/sync_lender.rs:118-138; crates/shortwin-math/src/pool.rs:598-600, 1459-1502, 1660-1690
seam: execution×first-principles
code_smells: Each current-epoch touch floors the interval credit and advances its snapshots without a fractional remainder.
description: An outsider can discard another lender's fractional credits with repeated sync calls; the review does not establish an economical attack.
trace: Shared SOL index advances → outsider calls sync_lender(0) for a current lender → touch_pot reaches touch_tail → snapshots advance after a floored credit.
proof: A current lender with 1000 shares and no forward chain receives floor(1000*delta/10^18). For two successive index increments of 5*10^14, a touch after each increment credits 0+0 lamports; one touch after both credits 1. Both pending and real use the floored interval product. touch_tail then assigns snap=pool.acc and snap_r=pool.acc_r, so the lost fractions cannot reach a later claim. A pool with 2000 shares obtains each increment from one released lamport. The owner need not sign: sync_lender intentionally permits the current-epoch touch through touch_pot. The rebase restriction and unchanged-record postcondition both pass because no conversion occurs.
guards: A second sync at an unchanged index loses nothing. The index must advance between touches. The owner and market keys still match the lender PDA. This lead does not bypass the owner-only rebase conversion.
limitations: The trace demonstrates frequency-dependent accounting. It does not establish profitable extraction, large losses per call, or a particular live pool's index cadence. The forward-chain branch uses cumulative floors and is not the branch identified here.
fix_direction: Retain per-lender fractional credits or use a cumulative accrual calculation that remains correct across share changes.
